selection.why: Round3 is significantly better on median case span (-57.52%), mean case span (-59.31%), and waiting (-98.26%), while service falls only 2.35%; utilisation also falls 37.64% but has no directional verdict. It is the strongest across-measure result, though it represents both substantially less queueing and slightly less work performed.
selection.gain_reading: both — the plan has significantly less waiting (98.26% lower) and significantly less service work (2.35% lower), with EXC-001 attributing -13.0774 activity hours per case; the payload does not provide absolute case-span or waiting hours, so those reductions cannot be stated as hour totals.

note: `best` is the best MEASUREMENT in the run, which is usually not the last round. ⚠️ `statistically_tied_with_best` is the SELECTOR'S CANDIDATE POOL, not a set of indistinguishable results: a row is admitted either because it is not significantly worse than `best` on the median, or because it is decisively better on ONE directional measure while possibly far worse on the others. Read each row's `admitted_because` before describing it, and never call the list a tie. `per_candidate` is the winning plan's own account: what each surviving candidate contributed on waiting, duration, throughput and resources.
